title: Vertical Diet Recipe Integration
description: Complete guide for integrating Stan Efferding's Vertical Diet recipes with the Tandoor/FatSecret meal planning system

overview.what_is_vertical_diet: The Vertical Diet is a performance-based nutritional framework created by Stan Efferding. It emphasizes easily digestible foods to optimize nutrient absorption and athletic performance. The diet focuses on red meat, white rice, and low-FODMAP vegetables.
overview.recipe_collection: data/vertical-diet/vertical_diet_recipes.json contains curated recipes from the Vertical Diet, including the famous Monster Mash and variations.
overview.goal: Enable seamless import of Vertical Diet recipes into Tandoor, automatic nutrition calculation, and sync with FatSecret for meal tracking.

data_flow: 1. Vertical Diet recipes stored in JSON format (data/vertical-diet/)
2. Import script reads recipes and calls tandoor_create_recipe binary
3. Recipes created in Tandoor with proper structure (steps, ingredients, keywords)
5. Recipes available for meal planning and FatSecret sync via sync_meal_plan

key_binaries.tandoor_create_recipe: Creates recipe in Tandoor from JSON structure
key_binaries.sync_meal_plan: Syncs meal plan entries to FatSecret diary

recipe_format.description: Vertical Diet recipes follow Tandoor's SourceImportRecipe format

structure.name: Recipe name (string, required)
structure.working_time: Active cooking time in minutes (integer, optional)
structure.keywords: Array of keyword objects with 'name' field
structure.nutrition: Nutrition facts object (optional, calculated if not provided)

import_all_recipes.description: Imports all Vertical Diet recipes into Tandoor
import_all_recipes.output: Logs success/failure for each recipe, creates log file in logs/vertical-diet-import/
notes: Script adds 'vertical-diet' keyword to all recipes for easy filtering
Includes 0.5 second delay between recipes to avoid API rate limits
Creates detailed log file with timestamps

import_single_recipe.description: Import a single recipe using tandoor_create_recipe

recipe.name: Monster Mash (Classic)
recipe.description: Stan Efferding's signature Vertical Diet meal

calculate_nutrition.description: After importing, calculate nutrition for recipes
calculate_nutrition.notes: Uses FatSecret API to lookup nutrition for each ingredient and calculate totals

sync_to_fatsecret.description: Add recipes to meal plan and sync to FatSecret
workflow: 1. Create meal plan entries with recipe names and servings
2. Use sync_meal_plan binary to sync entries to FatSecret diary
3. Entries appear in FatSecret app with proper nutrition tracking
sync_to_fatsecret.example: See examples/sync_meal_plan_basic.json for meal plan entry format

macros.protein: 1g per pound of bodyweight - primarily from red meat
macros.fat: 0.3g per pound of bodyweight - from butter, beef tallow, ghee
macros.carbs: 50-60% of total calories - primarily white rice and potatoes

food_emphasis: Red meat (beef, bison) - highly bioavailable nutrients
White rice - easy to digest carb source
Bone broth - minerals and gut health

monster_mash_variations: Monster Mash (Classic) - 438 cal, 32g protein per serving
Monster Mash (High Calorie) - 890 cal, 65g protein per serving
Bison Monster Mash - 380 cal, 34g protein (leaner option)
main_dishes: Grass-Fed Steak with Rice and Spinach
breakfast: Sweet Potato Hash with Ground Beef

workflow: 1. Import Vertical Diet recipes into Tandoor
3. Create meal plan with desired recipes
4. Use sync_meal_plan to log meals in FatSecret
5. Track progress and adjust macros as needed

meal_types.breakfast: Morning meals, typically eggs or breakfast hash
meal_types.lunch: Midday meals, often Monster Mash or steak
meal_types.dinner: Evening meals, larger portions for athletes
meal_types.snack: Between-meal additions to hit macro targets

solutions: Check logs in logs/vertical-diet-import/ for detailed errors

nutrition_calculation_fails.symptom: Recipe imported but nutrition is 0 or missing
possible_causes: Ingredient names not found in FatSecret database
solutions: Use more generic ingredient names (e.g., 'ground beef' instead of 'ground beef, 93% lean, grass-fed')
Refresh OAuth tokens using OAuth flow
Use only: breakfast, lunch, dinner, or snack

testing.integration_tests: Workflow tests cover meal plan sync (test_workflows.rs)
manual_testing: 1. Import one recipe: Use jq to extract first recipe and pipe to tandoor_create_recipe
2. Verify in Tandoor UI: Check recipe appears with correct steps and ingredients
4. Create meal plan entry: Use sync_meal_plan with the recipe
5. Check FatSecret: Verify entry appears in diary with correct nutrition
testing.test_data: examples/ directory contains sample inputs for all binaries
